_readme: State file for scripts/reconcile_catalog.py --watch.
The watch exits non-zero on any finding that is NOT covered here, which is
what turns the Catalog watch workflow red and sends the failure email. So a
red run always means something genuinely new. Silence means nothing changed.
THREE SECTIONS
acks  — one exact finding key, e.g. "missing_single:711520". Use for a
specific product we have looked at and decided about. An optional
`until` date EXPIRES the ack and re-alerts, which is how
"revisit when Q3 ships" becomes a mechanism instead of a promise.
rules — a regex over the finding's name, scoped to one kind. Use for a
whole class we deliberately do not model, so a new member of that
class never re-alerts. ALWAYS set `kind`: a kindless rule silences
its pattern across every check, which is how a missing SET gets
swallowed by a rule written for sealed inserts.
reviews — the parts of the catalog no feed can watch: Japan Core legality
(a Japanese retailer's HTML), pins and lore counters (a fan site),
next set's spoilers (press releases). Each becomes a finding on its
`due` date and rides the same red run and the same email. `how` is
printed IN the alert, so the steps travel with it.
EVERY ack and rule needs a real `why`. This file is a decision record — an
entry with no reason is indistinguishable from sweeping something under the
rug, and the next person cannot tell whether it is still true.
Use the CLI rather than hand-editing, then commit the file:
python scripts/reconcile_catalog.py --ack missing_single:711520 --why "..." [--until YYYY-MM-DD]
python scripts/reconcile_catalog.py --done japan-core --next 2027-02-05

rules.why: Pack-insert puzzle pieces. 79 SKUs and growing one set at a time; we model the finished Ravensburger puzzles (SEALED_PUZZLES) but not the insert fragments. Revisit only if we decide to track inserts as a collectible class.

Pack-insert collectible cards (RoJ 19, Archazia 20, Winterspell 9, Whispers 18). Same call as the puzzle inserts — a category we have never modelled. NOT the spin-dial lore counters, which we now track in the Sealed collection.
Reign of Jafar Hourglass/Gray/Red inserts — same insert class as above.

missing_single:714566.why: Stand Out (Foil), Promo Cards #11. Read as a separate foil promo printing, exactly like the Mother Knows Best pair (711519 #1 / 711520 Foil #13): a '(Foil)' listing at its own number in this group, not the foil of a card we hold. It cannot be C2 #15's foil — YEAR3_PRINTING_BY_NUMBER declares #15 normal, and C2 cards exist as exactly one printing per collector number. So this one IS the promo-printing question and is blocked on the promo-printing-policy review due 2026-09-28, same as 705078-705082 and 711519/711520. No until: that review is the mechanism. Worth one check when the policy lands — whether it is instead C2 #11, a number we do not appear to hold.

missing_single:714954.why: Buzz Lightyear - Space Ranger (JP Exclusive), Promo Cards #63. NEW CLASS, needs a real decision rather than a precedent. Japanese exclusives are modelled today by JAPAN_ONLY_NONFOIL — a name-to-local-image map giving null prices, a local image and no TCGplayer link — on the stated premise that they are 'deliberately has no TCGplayer listing' (see card_no_pid:Promo Set 1|41). A JP exclusive with a live TCGplayer SKU, and therefore a real price, contradicts that premise. Decide with the promo-printing policy on 2026-09-28: either JP exclusives that get listed graduate to ordinary priced cards, or the map stays and this stays out. NOT VERIFIED whether we already hold this card at all — TCGCSV and the DB were unreachable from the session that filed it.

So it never needed the promo-printing-policy call. Staged as a REPRINT_PROMOS clone (base 702655 -> AVP #15, promo pid 705084) in patch_pid_overrides.py; clears itself once that script runs. Re-alerts on this date if it never did.

missing_single:705085.why: Rapunzel - Escaping the Tower (Store Championship), printed 16/P4 - the Top-8 winner's Holofoil copy to 705084's participant promo. Same resolution: staged as a REPRINT_PROMOS clone (base 702655 -> AVP #16, promo pid 705085). Printed numbers came from the card face (16/P4) and a retailer listing for the participant (15/P4), NOT from the TCGplayer 'Promo Cards' numbering, which is a different series - that group holds several unrelated numbering runs, which is why its #15/#16 are the C2 Challenge cards filed as 712024/712025. That distinction is why only this pair could be resolved and the other promo-printing acks still need their printed numbers established.

reviews.what: Prestage the next set's revealed cards before Lorcast indexes them
reviews.why: Lorcast publishes a set weeks after spoiler season starts, and TCGplayer lists sealed months early. Between those, revealed cards exist everywhere except on Packs.Ink. unbound_group catches the set itself; nothing catches its cards.
reviews.how:
Check the official site + Mushu Report/LorcanaPlayer for revealed cards.
Run scripts/prestage_set_cards.py for any with a confirmed collector number.
Cards with a name but no number are NOT prestageable — wait for the checklist.
Next up: Hyperia City (set 14), previews 2026-10-16, ships 2026-10-23.

reviews.what: Refresh JAPAN_CORE_PARTIAL_NUMBERS + the fully-released set list
reviews.why: Japan skipped sets 10 and 11 as standalone releases; their cards trickle out through the Curator's Library pack slot, a new wave per Japanese set. Nothing publishes that list — not Ravensburger, not Lorcast — so the filter silently drifts out of date until someone re-scrapes it.
reviews.how:
Scrape lorhappy.com categories ct139 (Whispers, JA-10) + ct140 (Winterspell, JA-11),
regex the `N/204 JA-1x` collector numbers out of the product titles, UNION them
into JAPAN_CORE_PARTIAL_NUMBERS in Index.html (never replace — a retailer can be
out of stock on a card).
Also add any set that has since released in Japan to JAPAN_CORE_FULL_SETS.
Plain curl works there with a browser UA; lorcanaplayer.com is Cloudflare-blocked.
See the project_japan_core_legality memory for the full method.

reviews.what: Check for new pins and lore counters, and photograph them
reviews.why: One pin per League/Weekly Play season plus one lore counter per season and per Illumineer's Trove, so a new set means roughly 3-4 new collectibles. The lists are static data in Index.html (LORCANA_PINS / LORCANA_LORE_COUNTERS) with no feed behind them at all.
reviews.how:
Compare against lorcanaplayer.com/disney-lorcana-pins/ and /disney-lorcana-lore-counters/
(Cloudflare-blocked to curl AND to a headless browser — use a fetch tool. The Weekly
Play counters are not in that page's HTML at all; product-sitemap.xml enumerates them
and each /product/ page carries the photo path.)
Append with the NEXT FREE `n` — never renumber. `n` is the owned-mark key AND the
photo's filename, so renumbering both moves someone's collection and repoints art.
PHOTOS (done for all 62, 2026-08-24, with Lorcana Player's permission): download from
i0.wp.com/lorcanaplayer.com/wp-content/uploads/... (their own host 403s; that Jetpack
mirror serves the same bytes), then:
  python scripts/cut_collectible_bg.py --in <dl> --out <cut> --contact sheet.png
  python scripts/upload_collectible_photos.py --pins <cut> --counters <cut> --commit
LOOK AT THE CONTACT SHEET. The cut fails per-image and silently.
Still open: Wilds Unknown has no counter in either list. Source hole, or real gap?

reviews.what: Reconcile set_aotv_promos' fabricated numbering, then decide whether Packs.Ink tracks promo PRINTINGS as separate priced items
reviews.why: Thirteen acked missing_singles are blocked on this call. It got BIGGER on 2026-09-10: chasing printed collector numbers for the backfill established that set_aotv_promos is not one series renumbered, it is THREE series flattened into a made-up 3-10 run. Confirmed off printed cards / retailer listings: Vixey is 4/PD1 (prerelease), Maleficent - Exultant Spellcaster is 4/DIS (Disney Parks) but we store it at #9, and Tigger - Hunny Barbarian is 12/P4 (buy-a-box) but we store it at #10. So our AVP collector numbers are partly invented, and at least one real number COLLIDES with an invented one: Meilin Lee is 10/P4, which is where Tigger currently sits. That is why the backfill was not done — writing 13 entries into a set whose numbering is wrong would compound it, and cn is identity here. The Rapunzel pair at 15/P4 + 16/P4 is unaffected: those are genuine P4 numbers and nothing else occupies them.
reviews.how:
STEP 1, and it now gates the rest: reconcile set_aotv_promos. Establish each
existing row's real printed number AND series off the card art, then decide whether
PD1 / P4 / DIS are one set or three. This answers the old 'are AVP and PD1 one series
we split in two' question — they are not, and neither is DIS.
Known so far (verified 2026-09-10): Maleficent 4/DIS (stored #9), Tigger 12/P4
(stored #10), Vixey 4/PD1 (stored #4, number right by luck), Rapunzel 15/P4 + 16/P4,
Belle - Always Reading 13/P4; Morph #9, Meilin #10, Randall #11 reported as P4 but
not yet confirmed off a card face.
STEP 2, the original question: do promo printings get their own priced tile?
Options: (a) EXTRAS_MAP entries, (b) CUSTOM_VARIANTS clones, (c) keep ignoring them,
(d) REPRINT_PROMOS in patch_pid_overrides.py — which is what AVP #9/#10, all six CC1
cards and now the Rapunzel pair actually ship on. So (d) is already the de facto
answer; the live question is which printings earn a tile and what distinguishes two
tiles of one card.
reconcile_catalog.py now classifies these automatically: a missing single whose name
matches a card we hold is reported as a promo printing of it, with the base pid and a
near-complete REPRINT_PROMOS line. Only the printed number is left to a human, which
is the part no feed carries.
Worth settling in the same sitting: the three Set Championship pairs (P3 #33/#34, P3
#53/#54, AVP #15/#16) render as two same-named tiles separated only by collector
number and carry no variant_label, so 'store championship' finds none of them.
Settle the JP-exclusive case too (missing_single:714954, Buzz Lightyear - Space
Ranger): JAPAN_ONLY_NONFOIL gives regional cards null prices and no TCGplayer link on
the premise they are never listed, and that premise now has a live counter-example.
Decide BEFORE Q3 prestaging on 2026-10-02, or it gets done twice.

reviews.what: Re-pull Ravensburger's brand bundle and re-bake Logos/lorcana/
reviews.why: Every set logo, ink badge, promo stamp and card glyph on the site is baked out of Ravensburger's official brand bundle, and the bundle only changes when they hand out a new one — there is no feed, no version number and no notification. So a set ships, its logo is simply absent for weeks, and nothing anywhere goes red: lorcanaSetArt() returns null and every call site renders the set's NAME instead, which is correct behaviour and therefore invisible. The set tile just quietly stops matching the twelve beside it.
reviews.how:
Ask Zaven for the current bundle (he is on the distribution list; a Google Drive
link is the usual form). Unzip it anywhere, then:
  python scripts/bake_brand_assets.py --bundle "<...>/Complete Bundle" --check
--check writes nothing and NAMES any file that moved — Ravensburger renames
between drops ("Set6_Colour" one set, "AzuriteSea-Color" the next), so fix the
manifest at the top of that script first and re-run until it is clean.
Then bake for real with --contact and LOOK AT THE SHEET: a logo whose alpha is
empty, or a 'white' glyph that was actually black, both bake without an error
and are invisible on exactly one theme.
Add the new set to LORCANA_SET_ART in Index.html (key = the SET_RELEASE_DATES
name), then `node scripts/test_brand_art.mjs`, which checks the maps against the
files in both directions.
Also worth a look each time: new promo stamps in Promo Icons/ for any promo set
we track, and whether the new set brought a colour logo for The First Chapter
(it is the one set with none, and ships as an inverted black SVG because of it).
